o: Perform unsigned binary addition using carry bits.
Apply logical left and right shifts, inserting zeros.
Explain overflow and loss of bits in fixed-width values.
c: 0+0=0; 0+1=1; 1+1=10, so write 0 and carry 1 into the next column.
Line up bits, add each column including any carry, then record the output.
A logical shift moves bits left or right and fills empty positions with zeros. The booklet shortcut is left ×2^n and right ÷2^n for unsigned numbers, subject to lost bits and integer results.
With fixed eight-bit storage, a carry beyond bit 7 is lost (overflow); bits shifted out are discarded.

challenge.coreHint: Write down the bits, shift the required number of positions, fill vacancies with 0.

stretch.task: Change the original value to 13. Predict the result of shifting its eight-bit form left twice, and explain the arithmetic shortcut.
stretch.hint: 13 is 00001101. Each left shift doubles the value when no significant bit is lost.

mastery.task: A student shifts 11000001 left by two places in an eight-bit register. Give the result, identify the bits lost, and explain why simply multiplying by four gives a different value.
mastery.hint: Discard the leftmost two bits before filling two zeros on the right.
mastery.answer: 11000001 << 2 gives 00000100 (4) in eight bits. The leading 11 is discarded. 193 × 4 = 772 cannot fit in eight bits: overflow occurs.
